observation.visible_scene: A top-down view of dry, footprint-marked sand. A dark fence/railing shadow lies across the lower-left and stays fixed. Near the center-right a small yellow object with a sharp cast shadow sits in the sand. A translucent amber object with a white ribbed/striped face is the main moving element.
visible_changes: From t=0.00 to about t=2.00 the ribbed amber object translates steadily rightward (and slightly downward) across the sand, closing the gap to the yellow object's location; the yellow object and the background footprints remain in place during this interval.
Around t=1.92–2.00 a large soft shadow (consistent with a person) enters from the right edge; the ribbed object now overlaps the yellow object's position.
At t=2.08 a sudden radial spray of sand erupts around that spot, opening a dark crater; the ribbed object is now seated inside the crater and the yellow object is no longer clearly distinguishable.

From t=2.08 to t=3.20 the starburst of airborne sand expands outward from the crater rim and then gradually thins/settles; the ribbed object stays lodged in the hole, and the fence shadow and surrounding footprints do not move.
The camera view itself does not pan or zoom; all apparent motion is object motion plus the sand spray.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the sand eruption or whether the ribbed object's rightward motion is what preceded it is not shown.
The fate of the yellow object (displaced, buried, or occluded) after the burst is not visible.
Whether the ribbed object settles further or is removed after t=3.20 is beyond the excerpt.
uncertain_details: The exact material/identity of the ribbed amber object is unclear.
It is uncertain whether the yellow object is covered by sand or pushed out of view during the burst.
The right-edge shadow's source is inferred only from its shape; no body is visible.
